items.text: Credit report must provide merged credit information from the 3 major national credit repositories
Credit reporting agency must be Experian, TransUnion, or Equifax
Credit report must include verification of all credit references provided on the loan application
Credit report must certify the results of public record searches for each city where the individual has resided in the last 2 years
Credit report may not reflect a security freeze and must be resolved

If a borrower unfreezes his or her credit after the date the original credit report was ordered, a new three-bureau merged report will be obtained to reflect current and updated information from all repositories
Housing Events and bankruptcies in the most recent 2 years must be explained by the borrower with a signed letter of explanation

If the disputed account has delinquency within two years of the credit report date and the account balance is over $2,500, the credit file should be documented with a credit supplement showing the dispute has been resolved
A tri-merge or Residential Mortgage Credit Report (RMCR) is required for all borrowers on a loan
A signed letter of explanation from the borrower is required for all inquiries within the most recent 90 days for debts not already shown on the credit report
If new credit was granted from inquiries within the most recent 90 days, documentation must be obtained to support the current balance and payment
Monthly payment for new credit from inquiries within the most recent 90 days must be included in the DTI
Minimum of 2 credit scores are required
3 Credit References covering the most recent 12 months from the date of the application, supported with canceled checks or bank statements
It is permissible to combine trades from the credit report with non-traditional credit to meet the tradeline requirement
All derogatory revolving and installment accounts 60 days delinquent within four years of closing require a full explanation

3 tradelines reporting for 12+ months with activity in the last 12 months, OR 2 tradelines reporting for 24+ months with activity in the last 12 months, OR 24 month mortgage history reporting on the credit report with a 0x30x12 history
The tradeline must be reflected on the borrower's credit report
The account must have been active in the past 12 months and may be opened or closed
Tradelines used to qualify may not exceed 0x60 in the most recent 12 months
An acceptable 12 or 24 month housing history not reporting on credit may be used as a tradeline
Credit lines on which the borrower is not obligated to make payments on are ineligible tradelines
660 score, minimum 2 scores required
There are no additional minimum tradelines that are required provided the above guidelines are met

source_headings: AGE OF APPRAISAL AND APPRAISAL UPDATES

items.text: Appraiser must provide his or her license or certification on the appraisal report
Appraisals must be completed by appraisers who are properly licensed or certified in the state in which the property to be appraised is located
Appraisal must use Uniform Residential Appraisal Form for One Unit Properties (FNMA Form 1004)
Appraisal must use Small Residential Income Property Appraisal Report for 2-4 Unit Residential Properties (FNMA Form 1025)
Appraisal must use Individual Condominium Unit Appraisal Report (FNMA Form 1073)
Single Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) must be included for all 1-unit Investment Properties when rental income is used to qualifying
1-4 Family Rider (Assignment of Rents) (FNMA Form 3170) must be included for all Investment Properties
Appraisal report must contain a street map showing the location of the subject property and all comparable used
Appraisal report must contain exterior building sketch of the improvements indicating dimensions
Appraisal report must contain a floor plan sketch with calculations demonstrating how the estimate for gross living area is determined
For a unit in a condominium project, the sketch of the unit must indicate interior perimeter unit dimensions rather than exterior building dimensions
Appraisal report must contain original color photographs or digital color images of the front, street, and rear views of the subject property
Interior photos of the subject are required to include the kitchen, all bathrooms, the main living area, any areas with physical deterioration, and any renovations/improvements
Appraisal report must contain analysis of all agreements of sale, options or listings for the subject property current as of the effective date of the appraisal
Appraisal report must contain analysis of all sales of the subject property that occurred within the 3 years prior to the effective date of the appraisal

Appraisal report must include a completed Sales Comparison Approach section of FNMA Form 1004 where there are comparable used with more than one sale or transfer in the 12 months prior to the effective date of the appraisal
Appraiser must provide comments on any unfavorable conditions, such as adverse environmental or economic factors, and how those conditions impact the market value of the property
When unfavorable conditions exist, the appraiser's analysis must reflect and include comparable sales that are similarly affected
Certification and Statement of Limiting Conditions signed by the appraiser must be included
The appraisal must be dated within 365 days of the Note date
A recertification of value is required if the report exceeds 120 days of the Note Date

When an appraisal report will be more than 4 months old (120 days) on the date of the Note and Mortgage, the appraiser must inspect the exterior of the property and review current market data to determine whether the property has declined in value since the date of the original appraisal
Appraisal Update and/or Completion Report (FNMA Form 1004D) must be used when updates are needed for 1-4 Unit Residential Properties
Inspection and results of the analysis must be reported on the Appraisal Update and/or Completion Report (Form 1004D)
A photograph of the front of the subject property must be included with Form 1004D
If the appraiser indicates on Form 1004D that the property value has declined, then the seller must obtain a new appraisal for the property

When substitute appraisers complete updates, the substitute appraiser must review the original appraisal and express an opinion about whether the original appraiser's opinion of market value was reasonable on the date of the original appraisal report
The seller must note in the file why the original appraiser was not used
Appraisal must use FHLMC 71A
Appraisal must use FHLMC 71B for loan amounts < $750,000
Narrative report is required
Full interior inspection of each unit is required
Rent roll must be included with the appraisal report
Income and Expense Statement must be included with the appraisal report
Photos of subject including exterior/interior and street scene must be included
Aerial photo must be included
Sketch or floor plan of typical units must be included
Map must be included
Appraiser's qualifications must be included
Appraisal order date may NOT be prior to initial signed dated borrowers Application and 'Intent to Proceed' issued with the initial application and disclosure package

source_headings: MORTGAGEE CLAUSE REQUIREMENTS BY PROPERTY TYPE
NOTICE OF CANCELLATION FOR PROPERTY INSURANCE
DETERMINING THE AMOUNT OF REQUIRED HAZARD COVERAGE
CONDOMINIUM AND PUD PROJECT INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS

items.text: Hazard insurance must protect against loss or damage from fire and other hazards covered by the standard extended coverage endorsement.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for fire or lightning.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for explosion.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for windstorm (including named storms).
Hazard insurance must include coverage for hail.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for smoke.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for aircraft.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for vehicles.
Hazard insurance must include coverage for riot or civil commotion.
Coverage must provide for claims to be settled on a replacement cost basis.
Property insurance policies that provide for claims to be settled on an actual cash value basis are not acceptable.
Policy must be effective for at least 60 days after the date of funding.
Evidence of Insurance may be provided in one of the following forms: Policy, Certificate of Insurance (COI), or Insurance Binder.
Names of borrowers on Evidence of Insurance must reflect the same as the names on the note.
Property address on Evidence of Insurance must agree with the note/security instrument.
Mailing address on Evidence of Insurance must be the same as property address.
Evidence of Insurance must provide Policy Number (NA on a binder).
Evidence of Insurance must provide Loan Number.
Evidence of Insurance must provide name of insurance company.
Evidence of Insurance must provide Insurance Agent information.
Evidence of Insurance must provide effective and expiration dates of coverage.
Evidence of Insurance must provide Premium Amount.
Evidence of Insurance must provide coverage amounts and deductible.
Evidence of Insurance must provide loss payee clause as applicable.
Evidence of Insurance must be signed and dated by agent.
The policy must require the insurer to notify in writing the named insured and mortgagee(s) before it cancels the policy.
Hazard insurance coverage must be in the amount of the lesser of: the unpaid principal balance of the mortgage or 100% Replacement Cost Coverage as stated on the policy declaration page.

If the unpaid principal balance or 100% Replacement Cost Coverage requirements are not met, coverage must be equal to at least 100% of the insurable value of improvements, as established by the property insurer through a Replacement Cost Estimator or equivalent.

If the policy does not cover the unpaid principal balance, have guaranteed replacement cost or a replacement cost estimate is not provided, a processor's certification verifying the insurer's coverage is equal to 100% of the insurable value of improvements as indicated by the insurance agent or representative is acceptable.
The applicable insurance policy must include (or have attached) a standard or union mortgagee clause (without contribution) in the form customarily used in the area in which the property is located.
A loss payable clause in lieu of a mortgagee clause is not acceptable.

If a unit owner or shareholder maintains an individual property insurance policy (as indicated by the project's legal documents) or if an individual property insurance policy is required for interior coverage, it must include the standard mortgagee clause.
If an individual flood insurance policy is required, it must include the standard mortgagee clause.
Processor's certification must include the insurance company's complete information.
Processor's certification must include subject property address.
Processor's certification must confirm the replacement cost amount determined by the insurer.
Processor's certification must be signed and dated by the processor.

source_headings: NAMED INSURED FOR PROPERTY AND FLOOD INSURANCE

items.text: Flood Certificate must be provided by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
Appraisal report must accurately reflect the flood zone
Property must be in a community which participates in the FEMA Program
Flood insurance is required when property is located in a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA), Coastal Barrier System (CBRS), or Otherwise Protected Area (OPA)

Flood insurance policy must be either a standard policy issued under NFIP or a policy issued by a private insurer if the terms and amount of coverage are at least equal to that provided under a NFIP policy based on a review of the full policy issued by the private insurer

Minimum flood insurance coverage must be the lower of: 100% of the replacement cost of the insurable value of the improvements, the maximum insurance available from the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) which is currently $250,000 per dwelling, or the unpaid principal balance of the mortgage
Flood insurance must be maintained throughout the duration of the loan
Evidence of Insurance must show names of borrowers that reflect the same as the note
Evidence of Insurance must show property address that agrees with the note/security instrument
Evidence of Insurance must show mailing address that is the same as property address
Evidence of Insurance must show Policy Number
Evidence of Insurance must show Loan Number
Evidence of Insurance must show Name of insurance company
Evidence of Insurance must show Insurance Agent information
Evidence of Insurance must show Effective and expiration dates of coverage
Evidence of Insurance must show Premium Amount and deductible
Evidence of Insurance must show Coverage amount
Evidence of Insurance must show Loss payee clause as applicable
Evidence of Insurance must be signed and dated by agent
Individual property or flood insurance policy must list all persons holding title to the subject property as named insured
Master property or flood insurance policy must designate the HOA as the named insured
Master property or flood insurance policy can specify an authorized representative of the HOA, including its insured trustee, as the named insured if the condominium's legal documents permit
Master property or flood insurance policy must designate the HOA as the named insured
A signed IRS 4506-C must be completed and signed by all borrowers qualifying as full doc.
The form must request the appropriate type of transcript based on the level of loan documentation (W-2s, tax transcripts, etc.).

Wage earner's employment and income documented through a FNMA DU Validation Electronic Verification of Employment vendor (i.e., Blend, Equifax, Experian, Finicity, Truework) is required as one option to satisfy income verification.
Transcripts executed for 1 or 2 years, depending on the qualifying doc type, are required as an alternative to electronic verification of employment.
The prior 1 or 2 years tax transcripts are required when the most recent year's transcripts are not available.
The prior year's transcripts are required when qualifying as a two-year full documentation and the most recent year's transcripts are not available.
Copy of the e-filing certificate for the most recent year is required when qualifying as a two-year full documentation and the most recent year's transcripts are not available.

Proof the check cleared for any taxes due, or proof of receipt of the tax refund, is required when qualifying as a two-year full documentation and the most recent year's transcripts are not available.
Tax Transcript reflecting 'No Record Found' is required when qualifying as a two-year full documentation and the most recent year's transcripts are not available.
The transcripts must be reviewed and compared to the qualifying income to confirm consistency.
The results from the transcripts should be equal to or greater than the income used to qualify the loan.
Any inconsistencies between the transcripts and the qualifying income should be addressed.
Loan must be covered by a title insurance policy that has been paid in full and is valid, binding, and remains in full force and effect.
Preliminary title must indicate that the final title policy will be issued after funding.
Title insurer must be qualified to do business in the state where the subject property is located.
Title insurer and policy must conform to Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac requirements.

Final title policy must be written on 2006 American Land Title Association (ALTA) standard form, ALTA short form, or ALTA form with amendments required by state law in states in which standard ALTA forms of coverage are not used or in which the 2006 ALTA forms have not yet been adopted, provided those amendments are acceptable to FNMA or Freddie Mac (FHLMC).
Title insurer must be duly authorized and licensed, as required, to issue title insurance in the state where the property is located.

Title insurer must be evaluated in accordance with the lender's procedures for title insurer approval, which may include factors such as an acceptable rating from a rating agency, financial strength of the title insurer, adequate reserves, or record related to satisfactory title claim resolution.
All files must contain a 24-month title history from an acceptable source.
Transfer date, price, and buyer and seller names on any title transfers that occurred within the previous 24 months should be provided.
Vesting history should be reviewed for inconsistencies or any indication of flipping activity.

Customary public utility subsurface easements are allowable title exceptions only if the location is fixed and can be verified, and the exercise of rights of easement will not interfere with use and enjoyment of any improvement of the subject property or proposed improvements upon which the appraisal or loan is based.

Above-surface public utility easements that extend along one or more property lines for distribution purposes, or along the rear property line for drainage, are allowable title exceptions only if they do not extend more than 12 feet from the subject property lines and do not interfere with any of the buildings or improvements, or with the use of the subject property.

Public utility restrictions are allowable title exceptions provided their violation will not result in the forfeiture or reversion of title or a lien of any kind for damages, or have an adverse effect on the fair market value of the subject property.

Mutual easement agreements that establish joint driveways or party walls constructed on the subject property and on an adjoining property are allowable title exceptions provided all future owners have unlimited and unrestricted use of them.

Encroachments of one foot or less on adjoining property by eaves or other overhanging projections or by driveways are allowable title exceptions provided there is at least a 10-foot clearance between the buildings on the subject property and the property line affected by the encroachments.

Encroachments on the subject property by improvements on adjoining property are allowable title exceptions provided these encroachments extend one foot or less over the property line of the subject property, have a total area of 50 square feet or less, do not touch any buildings, and do not interfere with the use of any improvements on the subject property or the use of the subject property not occupied by improvements.
Encroachments on adjoining properties by hedges or removable fences are allowable title exceptions.
Liens for real estate or ad valorem taxes and assessments not yet due and payable are allowable title exceptions.
Outstanding oil, water, or mineral rights are allowable title exceptions if they do not materially alter the contour of the property or impair its value or usefulness for its intended purposes.
Municipals and local searches, when provided, must be cleared/resolved prior to loan funding or purchase.
Iowa Title Guaranty is an acceptable title guarantor for properties located in the state of Iowa.
If surveys are not commonly required in a particular jurisdiction, an ALTA 9 endorsement can be obtained.
If neither a survey nor the ALTA 9 endorsement are customary in a particular location, title must not have a survey exception.
If the title company requires a survey or plat map due to an exception noted on the title policy, a copy must be submitted in the loan file.
Surveys must be certified, dated, and signed by the licensed civil engineer or registered surveyor performing the survey.
Unimproved land surveys are not acceptable.
Surveys should be reviewed for easements, encroachments, flood zone impacts, and boundary violations, based on the location of the dwelling on the property.
Government ID must verify the borrower's name
Government ID must verify the borrower's date of birth
Government ID must verify the borrower's address
Government ID must verify the borrower's identification number
Name on the ID must match the name on the loan application, credit report, and title documents
Business Purpose & Occupancy Affidavit is required on all Business Purpose loans
All borrowers are required to sign the Business Purpose & Occupancy Affidavit to declare that the property is, or will be, for commercial business or investment purpose only
The Property must not and cannot be occupied by a borrower, any member of the borrower's LLC, or any family member
Compliance Agreement – DSCR Loans or equivalent form is required
Form is borrower(s) agreement to furnish the Lender and its successors and/or assigns with current copies of all Lease Agreements within a reasonable time upon request
Compliance Agreement – DSCR Loans form will be executed at closing on retail and wholesale transactions
Compliance Agreement – DSCR Loans form is to be provided at the time of purchase on correspondent loans
The Business Rider to the Mortgage/Deed of Trust must be executed at closing on retail and wholesale transactions
Investment properties and all DSCR loans must be Business Purpose and processed as non-TRID transactions

Properties with expired leases that have been converted to month-to-month per the terms of the lease will require bank statements for the lesser of two months or the period after the lease has expired.
Corporate lease agreements are acceptable with lease terms consistent with typical market standards and will be subject to standard market rent verification.
Lease agreements that allow single room occupancy or boarder leases are not permitted.
Short term rentals are not permitted.
Third party sale and leaseback agreements or contract for deed transactions will not be permitted.
All leases must be in U.S. Dollars.

All units must be either leased or in lease ready condition meaning the properties have been cleaned, no renovations or repairs to the properties are needed and the properties are immediately available to be leased to an eligible tenant.
The term of the leasehold estate must run for at least five years beyond the maturity date of the mortgage unless fee simple title will vest at an earlier date in the borrower's name.

The lease must provide that the leasehold can be assigned, transferred, mortgaged, and sublet an unlimited number of times either without restriction or on payment of a reasonable fee and delivery of reasonable documentation to the lessor.
The lessor may not require a credit review or impose other qualifying criteria on any assignee, transferee, mortgagee, or sublessee.
The lease must provide for the borrower to retain voting rights in any homeowners' association.

The lease must provide that in addition to the obligation to pay lease rents, the borrower will pay taxes, insurance, and homeowners' association dues (if applicable), related to the land in addition to those he or she is paying on the improvements.
The lease must be valid, in good standing, and in full force and effect in all respects.
The lease must not include any default provisions that could give rise to forfeiture or termination of the lease, except for nonpayment of the lease rents.
The lease must include provisions to protect the mortgagee's interests in the event of a property condemnation.
The lease must provide lenders with the right to receive a minimum of 30 days' notice of any default by the borrower.
The lease must provide lenders with the option to either cure the default or take over the borrower's rights under the lease.
The mortgage must be secured by the property improvements and the borrower's leasehold interest in the land.
The leasehold estate and the improvements must constitute real property, be subject to the mortgage lien, and be insured by the lender's title policy.
The leasehold estate and the mortgage must not be impaired by any merger of title between the lessor and lessee.

In the event the mortgage is secured by a sublease of a leasehold estate, the documents must provide that a default under the leasehold estate will not by such default result in the termination of the sublease.
Leasehold condominiums are ineligible.

source_headings: RENTAL INCOME ON THE TAX RETURNS
RENTAL INCOME NOT ON TAX RETURNS
SHORT TERM RENTALS – DSCR SUPREME AND INVESTOR DSCR
LONG TERM RENTALS – DSCR SUPREME AND INVESTOR DSCR

items.text: Reduce qualifying rents by any management fee reflected on the appraisal report.
Use lower of estimated market rent or lease agreement.
Use the estimated market rent.
For leases that have been converted to month-to-month, provide 2 months bank statements to support rental income.
When Tax Returns are used for qualifying, rental income should be calculated using the FNMA Cash Flow Analysis Method.
When income is being qualified using two years, an average of income should be used unless the rental income is declining, in which case the most recent year's income should be used for qualifying.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Start with Gross Rents and Royalties received.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Less total expenses.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Plus Depreciation.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Plus Insurance.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Plus Mortgage Interest.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Plus Taxes.
Cash Flow Analysis of Schedule E: Plus HOA fees (if included on Schedule E).
Subtotal divided by 12 or 24 months depending on the doc type.
Primary Residence: This figure would be used as net rental income/loss and the full PITIA will be counted as a debt.
Rental Property: This figure less the proposed/existing monthly payment will be used to determine net rental income/loss.
Evidence of borrower's ownership of the property.
Lease agreement.
Two months bank statements demonstrating receipt of rental income.
Evidence the rental amount is at market rate, which can be documented via a 1007 or through an online source.
75% of the rental amount on the lease is used for qualifying.
Primary Residence: This figure would be used as net rental income/loss and the full PITIA will be counted as a debt.
items.condition: doc_type=no_tax_returns AND (loan_purpose=refinance OR property_type=other_REO) AND occupancy=primary_residence

items.text: Rental Property: This figure less the proposed/existing monthly payment will be used to determine net rental income/loss.
items.condition: doc_type=no_tax_returns AND (loan_purpose=refinance OR property_type=other_REO) AND occupancy=rental_property

items.text: 75% of the appraiser's opinion of market rent on FNMA Form 1007 or Form 1025, as applicable.
Primary Residence: This figure would be used as net rental income/loss and the full PITIA will be counted as a debt.
Rental Property: This figure less the proposed/existing monthly payment will be used to determine net rental income/loss.
75% of the rental amount on the lease if used for qualifying.
Evidence the rental amount is at market rate, which can be documented through an online source or a 1007.
Available on purchase and refinance transactions.
Short Term Rentals are properties leased on either a nightly, weekly, monthly, or seasonal basis.

All STRs require evidence from third party vendor (such as Property Guard, Vrolio or equivalent), validating that the governing municipality where the subject STR is located allows properties to be rented as STRs.
Option 1: Lesser of 1007/1025 completed using either long-term or short-term market rents.
When the 1007/1025 is prepared with the use of short-term rentals, the appraiser is required to address the seasonality of the subject property Short Term Rental market in computing the market rent.
If the appraiser fails to appropriately address for seasonality, gross rents should be reduced by a 50% vacancy.
On a refinance, a screen shot of the online listing must show the property is actively marketed as a short-term rental.
items.condition: rental_type=short_term AND program=non_DSCR AND income_option=1 AND loan_purpose=refinance

items.text: Option 2: 12-month lookback period to determine avg rents or annual or monthly statements from AirBNB or similar service.
Option 3: Tax Return along with a Schedule E.
For purchase transactions, it is acceptable for the property to be vacant.
Vacant properties on a refinance are not eligible.
If the property is currently tenant occupied, the 1007/1025 must reflect the terms of the lease.
Gross market rents are calculated using the lesser of the lease amount or market rents from the 1007/1025.
A copy of the lease is not required.
Property cannot be occupied by the borrower(s), any member of the borrower's LLC or any family member.
Short term rentals are ineligible.
Short Term Rentals are defined as properties leased on a nightly, weekly, monthly, or seasonal basis.
Min DSCR >= 1.15.
Max LTV: Lesser of 75% or the Matrix LTV/CLTV.

Evidence is required from a third party vendor (such as Property Guard, Vrolio or equivalent) validating that the governing municipality where the subject property is located allows properties to be rented as STRs.
1007/1025 or Alternative Short Term Rental Analysis developed by an AMC is required, regardless of how the STR income is computed.

Short Term Gross Rental Income Options: 1007/1025 or Alternative Short Term Rent Analysis form developed by an AMC or 12-month look back on rents received using bank statements or third party rental statements.
When using the 1007/1025 or alternative Short Term Rent Analysis, the market rents must account for the seasonality of the subject property's rents.
Not permitted in the five (5) New York City Boroughs.
FNMA 1007/1025 required.
items.condition: rental_type=long_term AND (program=DSCR_supreme OR program=investor_DSCR) AND loan_purpose=refinance

items.text: Executed lease with no less than 1 month remaining at the time of closing for all units in the subject property.
items.condition: rental_type=long_term AND (program=DSCR_supreme OR program=investor_DSCR) AND loan_purpose=refinance

items.text: Month to month tenancy is not subject to the 1 month remaining requirement with sufficient evidence to support continuance, such as a signed extension letter, bank statements to support deposits, or 1007/1025 which includes a review of the current lease(s) confirming month to month.
items.condition: rental_type=long_term AND (program=DSCR_supreme OR program=investor_DSCR) AND loan_purpose=refinance AND lease_status=month-to-month

items.text: Evidence property is listed for rent for vacant units.
items.condition: rental_type=long_term AND (program=DSCR_supreme OR program=investor_DSCR) AND loan_purpose=refinance AND unit_status=vacant

items.text: Statements must be consecutive and reflect the most recent months available.
The most recent bank statement used for the Bank Statement Analysis must be within 90 days of the Note Date.

Bank statements provided through a Fintech company working on behalf of the bank can be used provided the bank statement reflects the actual bank information, otherwise an internet search is required to confirm the relationship.
Asset Statements received via a third-party asset verification vendor must conform to the information that would be provided on bank statements.

Asset Statements received via a third-party asset verification vendor must be from a provider that is an authorized FNMA DU Validation vendor per the list at https://singlefamily.fanniemae.com/applications-technology/desktop-underwriter-validation-service/du-validation-service-verification-report-vendors.
Statements must support stable and predictable deposits.
Statements should show a trend of ending balances that are stable or increasing over time.
Excessive declining income or negative ending balances may preclude the borrower from bank statement eligibility at underwriter's discretion.
Any supporting documentation, such as a P&L statement used in conjunction with the bank statements, must align with the dates of the bank statements used for qualifying.
If personal bank statements provided reflect payments being made on obligations not listed on the credit report, See Undisclosed Debts for additional guidance.
ATM deposits may be included if a consistent pattern of deposits is present.
Deposits received directly from family members are considered non-business income and will be excluded.
Deposits received from businesses owned by family members will be considered on a case by case basis.
Decreasing or negative ending balances must be explained.
Any deposit deemed non-business income will be excluded from the income analysis.
Net transfers between accounts must be excluded when multiple accounts are used for qualifying.
Borrowers must be self-employed for at least 2 years.
The business must be in existence for a minimum of 2 years as evidenced by a letter from either the business tax professional, regulatory agency or licensing bureau.
The Employment Section of the application must include a minimum of 2 years employment history.
Non-Permanent Resident Aliens without U.S. Credit are ineligible.
Foreign Nationals are ineligible.
Non-Profits and Not for Profits are ineligible.
At least one of the borrowers must be self-employed.
All borrowers are required to be account holders of the bank accounts throughout the 12 or 24 months being used to qualify.
Verify the business is active and operating within 30 days of closing with either a phone listing and/or business address using directory assistance or internet search.
Tax returns and 4506-C are not required.
If Tax returns and/or Transcripts are provided, the loan will be ineligible.
Large deposits greater than 50% of the average gross deposits over a 12 or 24 month period must be sourced or excluded.
Transfers from other accounts on personal/comingled account statements must be documented or excluded.
Wire transfer deposits on personal account/co-mingled statements must be sourced as business income or excluded.
Only large deposits greater than 50% of the average gross deposits over a 12 or 24 month period which appear unusual, inconsistent, or non-business related must be sourced or excluded.

Transfers from other accounts on business account statements must be documented or excluded only if above the large deposit threshold, or if the deposits appear not to be business income (i.e., proceeds from a loan, online transfers from other accounts owned by the borrower, refunded expenses, tax refunds, another source of documentable income, etc.).

Wire transfer deposits on business account statements must be sourced only if above the large deposit threshold, or if the deposits appear not to be business income (i.e., proceeds from a loan, refunded expenses, tax refunds, another source of documentable income, etc.).
Borrower must be self-employed for a minimum of 18 months and must have a minimum of three (3) years prior experience in the same line of business.

Self-employed borrowers in a licensed profession (i.e., Medical, Legal, Accounting) will be considered from a business that has been in existence for less than two (2) years, but greater than one (1) year.
Borrower has at least three (3) years of documented previous experience in the same profession, or evidence of formal education in a related field.
Minimum 700 score required.
Max LTV of 80% for Primary Residence.
Max LTV of 75% for Second Home.
Max LTV of 70% for Investment Properties.
Ineligible for Express(DU) or Super Jumbo.
For borrowers who are independent contractors and do not necessarily own their own business, they must follow the co-mingled accounts guidance.
For borrowers who are independent contractors, evidence of filing tax returns and a Schedule C for 2+ years must be provided by their CPA / licensed tax preparer.
For borrowers who are independent contractors, an Expense Factor and/or P&L supporting their expenses must be provided.

In instances where an online listing or search is not possible due to the nature of the borrower's employment (i.e., consultants), verification of activity within 30 days of the note date can be provided via evidence of receipt of business income within 30 days of the note supported by either invoices, bank statements showing business deposits, or similar means to support the business' recent operation.
Borrower must intend to occupy the subject property for the majority of the year
Property must possess physical characteristics that accommodate the borrower's family
Property should be in the same general area as the borrower's employment, or additional documentation may be required at underwriter discretion to verify occupancy
Mortgage and rental payments not reflected on the credit report must be documented via an institutional Verification of Rent or Verification of Mortgage (VOR/VOM).
All mortgages and rental payments should be current at time of closing.
If the credit report or VOR/VOM reflects a past-due status, updated documentation is required to verify the account is current.
All months in which the borrower has rented and/or had a housing history must be documented.

Mortgage and rental payments on the subject and Primary Residence not reflected on the original credit report must be documented via an institutional third-party Verification of Rent or Verification of Mortgage (VOR/VOM).
The payment history for the primary residence and subject property must be current as of the funding date of the new transaction.

If the borrower is making payments to an individual or interested party, a VOM/VOR along with the consecutive most recent 6 months of canceled checks, bank statements, or Venmo/Paypal documentation is required.

Rent free is not eligible with the Second Lien Program.

items.text: Certificates of Deposits are eligible for closing costs, reserves, or asset utilization.

Copy of the borrower's canceled check is acceptable documentation for earnest money verification.
Certification from the deposit holder acknowledging receipt of funds is acceptable documentation for earnest money verification.
VOD or bank statement showing that the average balance was sufficient to cover the amount of the earnest money at the time of the deposit is acceptable documentation.
If funds were given over 12 months ago per the sales contract, then an escrow letter will suffice for sourcing of any funds given greater than 12 months from the closing date.
If the earnest money check has cleared the bank, bank statements should cover the period up to and including the date the check cleared the account.

A copy of the check that has not cleared may be obtained along with a processor's certification verifying with the bank the date the check cleared, the dollar amount of the check, and the individual providing the information.

Must be a Fannie Mae Selling System Report (SSR) with a score of 2.5 or less

Must support the appraised value for the transaction

Self-employed borrowers who are business owners paying their own earnings via a 1099 are not eligible to use this income documentation type

If the most recent 1099 is more than 90 days from the Note Date, one of the following must be provided: evidence of year-to-date earnings via YTD bank statements, a printout of YTD wages from the employer(s), or the lender's Verification of Employment (or similar form) with YTD income completed by each employer

If the 1099 is paid to the borrower's business rather than the borrower individually, an Expense Letter from the borrower's CPA/EA/PTIN-licensed tax preparer is required to determine the qualifying income

Large deposits are not required to be sourced on refinances or DSCR transactions

Documentation must include a one-month (or most recent quarterly) account statement showing opening and closing balances, borrower listed as account holder, account number, statement date/period, and current balance in U.S. dollars — or a Written Verification of Deposit completed by the financial institution — or verification via an approved third-party vendor
Non-borrowing parties on the account (excluding a non-borrowing spouse) must provide a written statement that the borrower has full access and use of the funds
All pages of any statement provided are required; summaries will not be accepted
For Foreign National using Asset Utilization, borrower must have the lesser of 1.5 times the loan balance OR $1,000,000 net of down payment, closing costs and reserves.
Qualified assets can be comprised of publicly traded stocks, bonds, mutual funds, the vested amount of retirement accounts, bank or investment accounts, and crypto-currency
Three months' seasoning of all assets is required (three most recent and consecutive statements)
All individuals listed on the asset account must be on the note and mortgage
Assets held in the name of a business are not eligible to be used for the asset utilization calculation
Asset statements utilized for asset utilization cannot be used to document any other income source

Assets held in a revocable trust are eligible only if the borrower is the trustee; assets held in an irrevocable trust are eligible only if the borrower is the beneficiary with immediate access to the trust assets

Qualified asset calculation: 100% of checking/savings/money market, 80% of publicly traded stocks & bonds, 70% of vested retirement accounts for borrowers 59½ or older (60% if under 59½), 100% of the pre-maturity surrender value of CDs (minus early-withdrawal penalty), and 60% of crypto funds based on current Coinbase valuation

Ineligible asset sources: business assets, unseasoned foreign assets, 529 college savings plans, proceeds from sale of real estate not seasoned 3 months, privately traded/restricted/non-vested stock, and assets that produce income already included in the income calculation

Net qualified assets = qualified assets less funds used for down payment, closing costs, and prepaids (when used as the sole source of income) or less funds used for down payment, closing costs, prepaids AND reserves (when used as supplemental income)
Depletion calculation methodology and resulting monthly income must be documented on the worksheet

Must specify the scope of documents/transactions the authorization covers

Must independently confirm the borrower's reported income source, amount, and frequency

Income amount and source must be consistent with what is reported on the loan application and used in qualification
Must be dated/current per the applicable documentation-recency requirements for the loan's income documentation type
Must be an institutional Verification of Rent (VOR) from the landlord or property management company, unless the borrower pays an individual/interested party
